verses.text: People of Israel, do not celebrate like the other nations. You have been unfaithful to your God. You love the pay of a prostitute on every threshing floor.
The threshing floors and winepresses will not feed the people. The new wine will fail them.
They will not stay in the LORD's land. Ephraim will go back to Egypt. The people will eat unclean food in Assyria.

They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD. Their sacrifices will not please Him. Their food will be like food at a funeral. Everyone who eats it will become unclean. Their bread is only for their own hunger. It will not come into the house of the LORD.
What will you do on the day of the holy festival? What will you do on the day of the LORD's feast?
Look, they run away from destruction. Egypt will gather them. Memphis will bury them. Weeds will take over their silver treasures. Thorns will grow in their tents.

The days of punishment have come. The days of payback have come. Israel will know it. The people say: The prophet is a fool. The man of the Spirit is crazy. They say this because of your many sins and your great hatred.
The watchman of Ephraim is with my God. But a trap for catching birds is set on all the prophet's paths. There is hatred in the house of his God.
The people have become deeply sinful, as in the days of Gibeah. God will remember their guilt. God will punish their sins.

The LORD says: I found Israel like grapes in the desert. I saw your fathers like the first fruit on a fig tree. It was the tree's first season. But they went to Baal Peor. They gave themselves to that shameful idol. They became as hateful as the idol they loved.
The glory of Ephraim will fly away like a bird. There will be no births, no pregnancies, and no children conceived.
Even if they raise children, I will take every child away. Not one person will be left. How terrible it will be for them when I leave them.
I saw Ephraim like the city of Tyre, planted in a pleasant place. But Ephraim will bring out his children to the killer.
Hosea prayed: LORD, what will You give them? Give them wombs that lose their babies. Give them dry breasts.
The LORD says: All their evil began at Gilgal. There I came to hate them. Because of their evil deeds, I will drive them out of My house. I will love them no more. All their leaders are rebels.
Ephraim is struck down. Its root is dried up. It will bear no fruit. Even if they have children, I will kill the children they love.
My God will throw them away because they did not listen to Him. They will wander among the nations.

9.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Speakers are not marked in the KJV. Verses 1-9 and 17 are Hosea, verses 10-13 and 15-16 are the LORD, and verse 14 is Hosea praying. Verse 1 (prostitute), verse 7 (the people mock the prophet), verse 8 and verse 14 use hard Hebrew wording and need careful review.

verses.text: Israel is a spreading vine. It makes fruit only for itself. The more fruit Israel had, the more altars Israel built. The better the land became, the better the idols Israel made.
Their hearts are divided. Now they must pay for their guilt. The LORD will break down their altars. The LORD will destroy their idols.
Soon they will say: We have no king, because we did not fear the LORD. What could a king do for us anyway?
They speak empty words. They swear false oaths when they make agreements. So punishment springs up like poison weeds in the furrows of a field.
The people of Samaria will be afraid for the calf idol of Beth Aven. Its people will mourn over it. Its priests were so proud of its glory. They will mourn too, because the glory is gone.
The idol will be carried to Assyria as a gift for the great king. Ephraim will be put to shame. Israel will be ashamed of its own plans.
Samaria's king will be cut off like foam on the water.
The high places of Aven, where Israel sinned, will be destroyed. Thorns and thistles will grow on their altars. Then they will say to the mountains: Cover us. They will say to the hills: Fall on us.
Israel, you have sinned since the days of Gibeah. The people have stayed in that sin. Did war not catch the evil people at Gibeah?
The LORD says: I will punish them when I choose. Nations will gather against them. They will be tied up for their 2 sins.
Ephraim was like a trained young cow that loved to thresh grain. I spared her fair neck from heavy work. But now I will make Ephraim carry a rider. Judah must plow. Jacob must break up the ground.
Plant what is right for yourselves. Then you will harvest mercy. Break up your hard ground. It is time to seek the LORD, until He comes and pours out what is right on you like rain.
You have plowed evil. You have harvested wrong. You have eaten the fruit of lies. You trusted in your own way and in your many soldiers.
So a roar of war will rise among your people. All your strong cities will be destroyed, like Shalman destroyed Beth Arbel on the day of battle. Mothers were crushed with their children.
So Bethel will bring this on you because of your great evil. At dawn the king of Israel will be completely cut off.

10.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Speakers are not marked in the KJV. Verses 10 and 11 are the LORD speaking; the rest is Hosea. Check: verse 1 ('empty vine') is rendered 'spreading vine'; verse 6 'king Jareb' is rendered 'the great king'; verses 9, 10 and 11 use hard Hebrew wording ('two furrows' is rendered 'their 2 sins'; 'I will make Ephraim to ride' is rendered 'carry a rider') and need careful review.
